survey: A stage spotlight hanging from a lattice truss. A round clamp grips the lower chord of the truss. A short pipe drops from the clamp and bends forward through an elbow into a flat yoke bracket. The yoke runs across the top of the lamp body and down its right side, where a round tilt knob fixes it at the body's pivot point. The far yoke arm is hidden behind the body, which matches the camera angle. The lamp is a cylinder seen three-quarter from the front-left. Its front bezel holds three round lenses (yellow, cyan, red) in a triangle, and colored beams spread down-left from them. A short round housing or cable port sticks out under the rear of the body. Every part connects to the next one: truss, clamp, pipe, yoke, pivot knob, body. Nothing floats, no cable ends loose, and the light could hang and tilt as drawn. The three-lens front is a fair simplification of a multi-LED fixture.
